title: Signal Lake
concept: A volunteer radio operator keeps receiving a rescue call from a lake that drained thirty years ago.
setting: A ham radio shack, a dry lakebed with a drowned town's rooftops exposed.
conflict: Every rescue attempt to the lakebed reveals more of the town — and less of the way back.
escalation: Coordinates shift each night; Sasha finds Elliot's own callsign in the town's 1994 radio log.
reveal: Elliot was the operator who ignored the original call in 1994. The caller isn't asking to be rescued; it's offering Elliot a chance to stay.
ending: Sasha hears her grandfather's voice on the frequency now, calmly giving coordinates.
emotional_objective: Guilt, grief, and an eerie, beautiful setting.

hooks.line: My grandfather's radio picked up a rescue call from a lake that hasn't existed for 30 years.
The drowned town under the lake still has its lights on.
hooks.first_visual: Rooftops in dry mud, one window lit.

hooks.line: Who's still calling for help down there?
hooks.first_visual: Old CB handset on a dashboard in the mud.

hooks.line: We drove out to the coordinates.
The coordinates move every night. Closer to the house.
hooks.first_visual: Map with pins marching toward a cottage.

originality_review: Original. Drowned-town imagery is a real-world phenomenon; story is fictional and must not reference any real disaster.
